items.headline: Amazon aims for delivery drones to reach 500 US neighborhoods by end of 2026
items.facts: Amazon announced plans to launch Prime Air drone deliveries in several US cities, expanding service to up to 500 neighborhoods by 2026, which will increase noise for local communities.

framing.narrativeTitle: Amazon drone rollout and neighborhood noise
framing.publicBrief: Amazon announces Prime Air will begin delivering packages by drone in dozens of cities, aiming to cover up to 500 neighborhoods by the end of 2026. Residents in those areas hear the whir of rotors overhead and worry the constant buzz will disturb daily life. The company touts faster service, while local communities fear a loss of quiet.

roleFlavor.contributor: You represent Amazon, balancing the promise of rapid delivery against the complaints of nearby residents.

howItWorks: Amazon controls the deployment schedule and flight paths of the drones.
Local neighborhoods experience the noise but do not control the technology.
If Amazon proceeds without adjustments, drones will fill the sky over the selected areas.
If Amazon slows or modifies the rollout, delivery speed drops but noise levels stay lower.
missionCopy.choicePrompt: Decide how to proceed with the drone program

outcomes.COOPERATIVE: Amazon limits flights to quieter hours, preserving community peace while maintaining a reduced service pace.
outcomes.BETRAYAL: Amazon pushes full‑speed rollout, delivering to all 500 neighborhoods quickly but generating constant drone noise for residents.
outcomes.MIXED: Amazon pilots a partial rollout, delivering to some neighborhoods fast while others receive service later, creating uneven noise impact.
